about: What a script may write to a colour property, run by BOTH runtimes: colourPropertyCases.test.js through the editor's scriptColours.panelColour and colourFieldAt, and CE/tests/PanelValueModelTests.cpp through CE/src/Scripting/ScriptColours.h, which the plug-in reads a set() by with its window shut. Each case writes `value` to a field of kind `field` (see fields) on a panel whose control set has exactly the names in controlSetNames, and is either stored (what is stored) or refused (why and advice, the two halves of the sentence set() prints: set("<path>"): <why>, so nothing was set. <advice>). Each fieldCase asks whether `path` on the control `root` is a colour property, and of which kind; null means it is not one. Each controlSetCase asks whether a panel with that `controlSet` and `controlSets` resolves the reference `name`, as the editor's resolveToken(name, controlSetForPanel(panel)) answers and the plug-in's controlSetResolves must, against the real built-in and base sets.
